post.headline: For admins: do not ignore a forged sender warning
post.subtext: The Tools page can show when an email likely did not originate from the stated sender, giving teams a clear stop point before anyone acts on it.
post.image_alt_text: A Hush Line daily social asset built around a light-mode desktop admin screenshot of the Tools page. The Email Validation tab shows raw email headers, Validate Headers and Download Report buttons, and a Validation Summary warning that the email likely did not originate from the stated sender.

social.bluesky:
For admins running Hush Line: do not treat a forged sender warning as routine.

Email Validation can show when an email likely did not originate from the stated sender. Pause before staff act or reply.

Review safer handling steps at https://hushline.app.
social.linkedin:
A common mistake for teams running Hush Line is treating a forged sender warning like routine background noise.

For admins and deployment teams, the Tools page shows Email Validation with a Validation Summary that says when an email likely did not originate from the stated sender. Use that result as a stop point: slow down, keep the message out of ordinary staff action, and decide who should assess it before anyone replies.

For admins: review how your team handles forged sender warnings before the tip line is in regular use. Learn more at https://hushline.app.
